subject: Cloud Computing
title: Cloud and Startup Speed
description: A short lesson to help you apply Cloud and Startup Speed.

hook.text: In 2005, launching a tech startup required $1 million in servers. Today, it takes a credit card and $50.

buildup.text: Cloud eliminated the biggest startup barrier: upfront infrastructure cost. Ideas could go live in hours.

discovery.text: Instagram had 13 employees serving 30 million users — all running on AWS. That was impossible a decade earlier.

twist.text: The flip side: low barriers mean more competition. When anyone can launch, everyone does.

climax.text: Cloud democratized technology. The winners are now decided by ideas and execution, not capital budgets.

punchline.text: Cloud leveled the startup field. Now the best idea wins.

quiz.question: How did cloud computing change the startup landscape?
options: It eliminated upfront infrastructure costs, letting anyone launch quickly
It made startups more expensive to run than before
It required startups to build their own data centers first

details.summary: Cloud computing lets startups launch products in days instead of months, without buying servers or signing data center leases. This speed advantage means cloud is standard infrastructure for nearly every new technology company, giving startups access to enterprise-grade infrastructure from day one.
details.whyItMatters: Cloud fundamentally changed the economics of starting a company. The ability to launch with minimal capital and scale on demand removed traditional infrastructure barriers to entrepreneurship.
takeaways: Startups launch in days without buying physical infrastructure
Pay-as-you-go eliminates large upfront infrastructure investment
Enterprise-grade capabilities are available from day one

faq.question: How much does cloud cost for a typical startup?
faq.answer: Early-stage startups often spend $50 to $500 per month on cloud with free tier credits extending runway further. As the product scales, monthly costs grow to thousands or tens of thousands. Startup credit programs provide $5,000 to $100,000 in free credits.

faq.question: What cloud services do startups use most?
faq.answer: Managed databases, compute instances or serverless functions, object storage, CDN, email delivery, and authentication services. Startups favor managed services to minimize operational overhead and move fast. They optimize costs later when scale demands it.
